- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5) and prices are falling, model often overcorrects downward — adjust forecast upward to avoid excessive bearish bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots — reduce forecast in next 3–5 periods to reflect mean reversion.  
- If sentiment swings sharply from negative to positive within 5 days, model often fails to adjust forecast quickly — apply a lag correction: delay upward shift by 1–2 periods.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (first 5–7 days) — apply a small upward bias (e.g., +1–2% of recent mean) for first 5 days.  
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.3–0.5 over 3+ days), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior values before applying sentiment-weighted adjustment.
